discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind admission of one pinned six-harness resource-overhead batch. The benchmark uses a local scripted mock rather than a real model, three serial runs per harness, and reports the median run. W1 preserves process-resource measurements and publisher beta CU values without treating them as task-quality outcomes or universal efficiency scores.
discovery_pass.workload: 100 scripted tool-use turns; local protocol-matched mock; no real model inference

no real model identity exists for this benchmark

provenance_strength.w1_treatment: admit factual source-reported resource measurements; separate first-party peri provenance from externally measured harness rows

protocol_deviations_and_failures.detail: Renderer, repository validators, pass-40 admission checks, and existing live admission checks passed; generated registry views were uploaded as workflow artifact 11107102502.

Registry regeneration succeeded and the workflow token had contents:write, but actions/checkout had checked out the synthetic PR merge ref while the branch head advanced. The resulting generated commit could not fast-forward the PR branch. No raw evidence changed.
Standard repository validation correctly failed because append-only raw observations had been added while generated registry views were still stale.

The temporary workflow checked out the exact PR head branch, rendered 296 observations, fast-forwarded the generated registry commit, passed repository validators, pass-40 admission checks, and the existing live admission path.

GitHub did not automatically execute the workflow for the bot-authored generated-registry commit; this was superseded by explicit restoration of the standard workflow and a fresh read-only validation.
